title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Summary
text: Notarize physical documents in person, comply with state statutes, update commission info, and adhere to Cayman Bank’s guidelines for customers and non-Cayman Bank customers.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Notarizing at Cayman Bank locations
text:
If you need to obtain or renew a notary commission or need help with notary information including notary supplies, refer to Branch Portal > Branch Tools > Notary Information link.
Existing notaries new to Cayman Bank only: Complete the Employee Information for Existing Notaries New to Cayman Bank (597201) form and submit it to the National Notary Association (NNA) following the instructions on the form
An employee must have both a valid commission from their applicable state and current commission information listed on Banker Profile to perform notarizations at Cayman Bank locations.
Display signage (commission or license) if required by your state.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Notarizing at Cayman Bank locations
text:
All Cayman Bank branch employee notaries are covered by the corporate insurance program for Error’s and Omission’s (E&O) insurance while performing work in the scope of their job, including notary services.
Locations may limit to 50 notarizations or one hour of service per requester, whichever comes first. If a substantial request disrupts bank operations, an appointment should be scheduled for the remaining documents.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text:
Notary publics are commissioned by the state from which they obtain their notary commission, not Cayman Bank.
Employees commissioned as notaries are required to follow their applicable state statutes when executing notary duties. If there are questions requiring a deeper understanding of applicable laws or regulations, notaries should use the following resources for state-specific questions:Your state notary website from your Secretary of State or state agency National Notary Association (NNA) hotline at 1-888-876-0827
Employees who obtain or renew a notary commission must complete the affiant and notary training course through Develop You every other year.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text: Notaries must adhere to the following requirements when providing notary services:Cayman Bank Customers: Notarize both Cayman Bank documents and non-Cayman Bank documents. Note: A Cayman Bank customer is an individual who has transaction authority on any Cayman Bank account relationship. Non-customers: Notarize only Cayman Bank documents unless the notary’s state laws provide an exception. Exceptions: Notaries in Arizona, Iowa, New York, South Dakota, and Utah must notarize both Cayman Bank documents and non-Cayman Bank documents regardless of their customer status.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text: York, South Dakota, and Utah must notarize both Cayman Bank documents and non-Cayman Bank documents regardless of their customer status. If a customer requests a notarization on a non-Cayman Bank document that also lists other present individuals (non-customers) requiring a notarization on the same document, notaries may notarize all individuals’ signatures regardless of their customer status. Notarize documents only at a Cayman Bank branch during business hours. Do not go offsite to complete notarizations during business work hours to conduct bank business transactions. Notarize only physical documents presented in person by the requester. Do not notarize documents sent by email, fax, mail, or text, even if the requester is present.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text:
by the requester. Do not notarize documents sent by email, fax, mail, or text, even if the requester is present. Do not provide any legal advice related to notarizing a document. Do not charge a notary fee for:Notarizations completed at a Cayman Bank location. Notarizing Cayman Bank documents at a branch location or notarizing Cayman Bank documents outside Cayman Bank on your own personal time.
The notary must comply with state laws if asked to act as a notary and a witness on a single document.
Related procedure: Witness Customer Signatures and Sign Cayman Bank and Non-Cayman Bank Documents

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text:
For Cayman Bank Bank transactions, a notarized signature on a document is acceptable if one of the following entities either commissions or authorizes the notary or a person authorized by statute to sign the document:Any U.S. state Any U.S. Embassy or Consulate within a foreign country Any U.S. Territory (for example, Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, U.S. Virgin Islands, and the Northern Mariana Islands)
Note: Notarizations performed at a U.S. Embassy, U.S. Consulate, or U.S. Territory for customer identification purposes when opening a new account or completing relationship maintenance are only accepted for U.S. citizens.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text:
For documents requiring notarization for bank acceptance, do not accept those notarized by a notary in a foreign country (foreign notary) for Cayman Bank Bank transactions (for example, Power of Attorney).
Exception: They are acceptable for Cayman Bank Bank transactions if they meet the following conditions:
Obtain one of the following:Countries signatory to the Hague Convention: An apostille authenticating the notary's authority to perform the notarization. Countries not signatory to the Hague Convention: A certificate of notarial authority, or similar document issued by the foreign notary's governmental, authenticating the notary's authority to perform the notarization

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Understand the rules
text:
Note: Direct questions concerning the apostille or certificate of notarial authority, or how to obtain them, to the foreign governmental body.
Call Gateway to Team Member Support at 1-877-932-1852 say “document review” to review the document and apostille or certificate of notarial authority.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Complete the notary journal entry
text:
Cayman Bank requires using a bound notary journal to record all notarizations, even in states where notary statutes do not require a journal.
Only the notary may make changes in the notary journal.
A separate journal entry and customer signature is required for each document notarized.
Shield personal information from previous notarizations using a sheet of paper or similar object when obtaining the signature of the signer in the journal.
Related procedure: Information Security, Classification, and Compromised Data Incidents
Refer to the inside cover of notary journal for a sample on how to complete.

section: Complete the notary journal entry
text:
If permitted by your state, you may use a diagonal line (/) or ditto marks (") only when exact information repeats. However, do not use these in the signature or thumbprint sections.
Exception for California notaries: Do not use ditto marks or signatures across two spaces.
Complete the journal entry following your state-specific guidelines. For states not requiring a journal, the following fields are suggested to complete:

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Security requirements for notary supplies
text: Situation: Storing completed notary journals | Requirement: The notary must contact their applicable state agency (for example, Secretary of State) to confirm if there are any requirements related to storing completed journals. If there are no state requirements, it is recommended for the notary to store completed journals for 7 years from the last notarization date on each journal and then securely destroy them. Note: The notary does not need to store completed journals at a Cayman Bank location.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Security requirements for notary supplies
text: Situation: Notary is transferring to another location or is leaving Cayman Bank | Requirement: The notary must take their notary supplies (for example notary stamp and journal) with them. Note: If a notary leaves their stamp or journal behind, the manager must attempt to return them. If the supplies cannot be returned to the notary, the manager must complete the following:The notary stamp must be securely destroyed. Contact the appropriate Secretary of State or applicable state agency office for instructions on sending the journal(s) to the agency. If state statutes do not require the journals to be sent, retained them according to the Records Management > Retention Schedule. Document all steps taken with stamp and journals in the notary’s personnel file.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Notary commissions not renewed or are revoked
text:
If a notary commission is not renewed or is revoked, the notary must:
Contact their Secretary of State or applicable state agency office, for instructions related to the notary’s supplies (for example, notary stamp, notary journal) and revoking their commission.
Tell their manager of the non-renew or revocation. The manager can then update the notary’s Banker Profile.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Manager responsibilities
text:
Managers of notary employees or their designee must complete the following:
Monthly review:Ensure notaries use a bound notary journal for notarizations. Confirm the notary’s personnel file has required documentation on file (new, renewing, or transfer). Verify the Banker Profile certification tab includes current commission information. Ensure the notary’s personal and business contact information is updated with the state notary agency.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Manager responsibilities
text: Banker Profile Certification tab:Add or modify the notary’s commission number and expiration date when a notary's commission is obtained or renewed. Notes:Enter all 9s in the Commission Number field if the notary’s state does not provide one. The hiring manager updates commission details on the Banker Profile Certification tab for roving bankers. Delete the notary’s commission number and expiration date within 90 days of expiration or revocation.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Manager responsibilities
text:
Personnel File (new, renewal or transfer): Obtain and file a copy of the following documents in the employee’s personnel file:Notary’s commission from the state agency. Signed Cayman Bank Employee Notary Public Agreement. Note: File the documents at the employee’s primary work location if the employee is a roving banker.
Note: If the employee notary is a Roving branch employee, ensure the documents are filed at the employee’s designated home branch.

title: Notary: Services, Supplies and Manager Responsibilities - PR1000
section: Third-party external notary service
text:
Cayman Bank employees should use internal notary services (in branch or nearby locations) whenever possible.
If unavailable, use the approved email process and the mobile notary template to request an external notary for Cayman Bank documents at branch locations:
Direct contact with external notaries is not permitted.
48 hours' advance notice is recommended.

title: Secure Destruction, Store Materials and Records, and Record Holds - PR1263
section: Understand the rules
text:
Use secure destruction to protect the confidentiality of bank and customer information.
Shred vendors or secure-destruction services:Branches must use only the approved shred vendor or secure-destruction service selected for their region, or an approved in-location, cross-cut shredder. Management must ensure the approved vendor or service provides locking, secure-destruction bins or similar service containers for securely destroying dry trash. Do not remove documents or items from vendor-provided, secure-destruction bins.
Exception: In urgent situations, submit a Container Access Request to open the bin on Shred Services Order Forms. If dispatched, the vendor may submit additional charges.

title: Secure Destruction, Store Materials and Records, and Record Holds - PR1263
section: Understand the rules
text:
Secure-destruction bin keys:Retained by Shred Services, not by the branch. Cannot be assigned to, or in the possession of, employees. Do not give to contract employees or janitorial services.
Ensure secure destruction bins are:Not accessible to customers. Always locked and secured or under camera coverage within a Cayman Bank location (not in lobby areas). Chained or locked in the back of the retail location if the branch is without space for the bin. Not used for wet trash disposal (for example, break room and bathroom trash). Not overfilled where items can easily be removed.

title: Secure Destruction, Store Materials and Records, and Record Holds - PR1263

text: Note: If the bin is full and must be emptied before the scheduled pickup, submit an Off-Schedule Service Request on Shred Services Order Forms.

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Summary
text:
Determine if an individual’s identification meets the required criteria for primary or secondary identification.
Select the section heading to expand the procedure content.

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Understand the rules
text:
Review the identification requirements below to qualify as either primary or secondary ID.
The transaction ID requirements may vary for customers and non-Cayman Bank customers and by transaction type and amount.
Refer to the applicable procedure for specifics on the types of ID required for the transaction or service you are providing (for example, open account, account maintenance, teller transaction). Existing customers are encouraged to use these stronger forms of authentication when processing teller transactions and account maintenance: PIN validation with an inserted card or tapped card or device (phone, watch) One-time passcode (OTP) Acceptable types documented in the Identification Requirements - Teller Transactions procedure

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Understand the rules
text:
Do not accept a state-issued medical marijuana card as either primary or secondary ID.
A digital driver’s license is considered a companion document and does not replace the physical driver’s license requirement.
The primary and secondary ID cannot both be issued by the same entity (for example, DMV) and with the same ID number. Consider both documents to be the same ID (for example, state driver's license and state ID or nondriver's license issued by the same state). Obtain a different secondary ID.

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Understand the rules
text: If the individual provides an ID document with a signature for the requested transaction, compare the signature on the ID with the signature on the transaction document. It must favorably resemble the signature on the transaction document (for example, check endorsement or signed account application).

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Understand the rules
text:
A sovereign citizen is a member of a political movement of people who oppose taxation, question the legitimacy of government, and believe that they are not subject to the law. They may request to open an account with ID documents claiming to use laws outside of state and federal law. Cayman Bank cannot open accounts for these individuals, even if they are persistent or claim the Bank is acting illegally.
Refer to the CSBB 1FC Program Document for additional details on OFAC situations.

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Primary identification requirements (U.S. and Foreign)
text:
A customer’s U.S. or foreign-issued ID is considered a primary ID if it meets all of these requirements:
An original physical document (not a digital ID or copy)
Issued in the name of the individual presenting the ID
Contains a document or ID number
Printed in English Exception: Quebec driver’s licenses printed in French are acceptable for transactions processed on TellerView.
Not expired. An expiration date is not required, but if on the ID, it cannot be expired. (see U.S. ID exception)
Has a photograph that compares favorably with the individual presenting the ID (see U.S. ID exception)
The ID must meet the following requirements based on the issuing country:

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Secondary identification requirements
text:
ID not meeting the primary ID requirements is acceptable as secondary ID (or additional ID) if the ID meets all of these requirements:
An original physical document (not a digital ID or copy)
Issued in the name of the individual presenting the ID and matches the name on the primary ID presented
Printed in any language. Any branch employee can translate the ID’s foreign language or if unable to interpret, contact LanguageLine Solutions for assistance.
Not expired. An expiration date is not required, but if on the ID, it cannot be expired

section: Secondary identification requirements
text:

Issued by a business, education institution, or government entity. Examples include but are not limited to: Notes: The ID must meet all secondary ID requirements listed above. text:

The following are acceptable as secondary ID (without a signature or photograph): Birth certificate (minors only) Credit card or Debit/ATM card. A signature is not required. If one is present, verify the signature against the customer’s primary ID

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Identify customers with face coverings
text: When the customer presents a primary ID with a photograph or physical description, you must review and ensure the ID favorably resembles the individual presenting the identification. Exception: You can accept an unexpired state-issued ID card without a picture for individuals with religious beliefs prohibiting a photograph.

title: Primary and Secondary Identification Requirements - PR1277
section: Identify customers with face coverings
text:
Customer is wearing a face covering (for example, mask, bandana, or sunglasses) preventing you from positively identifying them: Tell the customer you cannot verify their identity using their photo ID and offer the following options: Temporarily remove the face covering. Cayman Bank customers may provide PIN validation with an inserted card or tapped card or device (phone, watch) when systematically available and permitted for the transaction requested.
You cannot positively identify a customer: Direct to a transaction approver to determine how to proceed.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text: The Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirement is designed to enable the bank to form a reasonable belief about an individual’s and nonindividual’s true identity for all new and existing deposit accounts, loans, financial products, contracts, safe deposit boxes, or any other type of banking service or product. The process of forming a reasonable belief is taking steps to verify the identity, credentials, identification, and other supporting information provided by potential and existing customers. You must provide the required disclosures, notices, and information to potential and existing customers.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
The Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirement enables Cayman Bank to know its customers and understand the nature and purpose of accounts and relationships to develop a customer risk profile.
Refer to the CSBB 1FC Program Document for additional details on Sanctions situations, UAR submission, CIP requirements, CDD requirements, and Beneficial Ownership requirements.
Compare the provided customer information to the customer identification (ID) or proof-of-entity documentation.
A completed Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must be obtained, certified, and signed by the customer at new account opening or business customer relationship maintenance to be valid and acceptable Reference: CIP and CDD Resources

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
When opening a business deposit account, at least one owner or key executive with entity authority and control must have a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) (for example, SSN or ITIN). If they do not, the business account cannot be opened.
A customer request to open a new deposit account must not be declined for the: Account may be open only a short time Customer has or will have duplicate accounts

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
Employees may open business deposit accounts for customers meeting the following criteria: Are nonindividual entity customers (including sole proprietorships, business trusts, business pension or profit-sharing trust, corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, joint venture, general partnerships, social and recreational clubs, unincorporated associations, and civic groups). Have gross annual sales of less than $2 million. Do not require Treasury Management Services. Do not have complex lending needs.
If the business does not meet the criteria, the employee must refer the customer to the appropriate partner or affiliate.
Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
Disclosures: If disclosures are not available, the account cannot be opened. A supply of disclosure New Account Kits (NAKs) may be obtained from another location. If the customer wants to receive the disclosure electronically and has access to their email through their mobile device, the account can be opened.
Employees must not sign or otherwise place a customer’s signature on a document on the customer’s behalf or in lieu of the customer physically signing. Print or digital copies of signatures obtained from the customer on previous documents must not be used when a signature is required on a new document.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779

text:
Employees are prohibited from entering into any customer provided agreements, up to and including agreements barring Branch Banking from sharing due diligence information with Financial Crimes Risk Management (FCRM), Internal Audit, regulators, or other similar functions. Any existing accounts with external agreements identified after account opening will be immediately exited.
When opening a new account for a business, the individuals who provide personal financial information in connection with the business must be given the opportunity to elect whether to share personal information with other Cayman Bank affiliates.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
Treasury Management deposit products are restricted from being offered to customers (for example, Controlled Disbursement, Stagecoach deposit). Only business account products can be opened by branch employees. Refer to the Products database for currently available accounts. Referrals must be directed to the appropriate partner or affiliate. Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates
Employees must not travel outside of the U.S. for purposes of conducting bank business or discussing bank related products or services.
A new account request must be blocked or restricted if the transaction is conducted by, for, or on behalf of countries, entities, or individuals affected by the Foreign Assets Control regulations.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
When the tax-responsible customer (for example, business account owner, third party, client, or insolvent party) is an entity, trust, or estate formed in a U.S. territory, a noninterest-earning product must be used.
Prohibited high-risk industries are not permitted to open or maintain deposit accounts or Safe Deposit Box Relationships.
Deposit accounts and Safe Deposit Box Relationships for restricted high-risk industries can be opened after they have been reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC).
Certain unregulated or unlicensed financial institutions are prohibited from being opened or maintained. These industries must be reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC) prior to opening the account.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
If a due diligence review is required, and the customer indicates either of the following, a Suspected Risk Referral (SRR) must be submitted, and a new account request must be denied: Refuses to provide information required to complete due diligence. Suspiciously indicates they provided the wrong responses to the compliance questions after the banker already disclosed the enhanced diligence requirements to the customer.
Multiple signature requirements are not allowed on a deposit account.
A fee waiver must not be placed on an account only because the customer has objected to the standard fees.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
A Pay on Death (POD) beneficiary may only be added to an account if the business entity is a sole proprietorship and is not an IOLTA, RETA, or public fund account. Other types of business entities (for example, corporations, partnerships, or limited liability companies) are ineligible for a POD beneficiary.
First deposit for new account: The minimum deposit requirement must be met and made at the time of the account opening.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.
Examples of court- or government-appointed fiduciary account types are:
Lottery
Attorney client trust
Business trust
Estate – Nonindividual personal representative
Real-estate trust
Representative payee
Individual and nonindividual guardian or conservator
Individual and nonindividual receiverships
Statutory client trust
Note: The minimum deposit amount is always required for a time deposit account.

Before opening a deposit account, risk screening must be completed on the following individuals: Owners with 25% or more ownership that have entity authority and control Key executives with entity authority and control
Note: Owners with less than 25% entity ownership with authority and control added to the business relationship will also be risk screened but it is not required.
Exception: Risk screening is not required for the following individuals:
Nonindividual owners with or without entity authority and control
Individual owners without entity authority and control
Key executives of a U.S. government unit or agency, or Indian tribal government

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Business trust, business pension or profit-sharing plan trust > Understand the rules
text:
Business Pension or Profit-sharing plan trust: A business pension or profit-sharing plan trust (for example, a pension plan, profit-sharing or 401(k) plan) has two components: the plan and the trust. The plan describes the benefits and IRS requirements. A plan administrator is appointed to make decisions for the plan. The plan is legally separate from the trust.
Note: People who are unfamiliar with retirement funds tend to use the words plan and trust interchangeably.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779

text:
The trust holds the plan funds. The trust has a trustee who is the individual with control over the trust and conducts transactions for the trust based on direction from the plan administrator. Accounts are opened in the name of the trust.
Note: The name of the plan may be the same as or different from the name of the trust.

text:
Open a receivership when a court appoints an individual or entity as receiver to take control of the assets of an insolvent party. The insolvent party may be an individual or nonindividual.
Note: A receiver is typically appointed to control the assets of a single insolvent party. In less common situations, a receiver may be appointed for multiple related insolvent parties.
The court document typically requires the receiver to close the insolvent party’s existing accounts and open a new account titled in the name of the receivership. The receiver may leave funds in the existing accounts to cover outstanding or known items to be paid.

When a new account in the name of the receivership is requested, a business product must be opened even if the insolvent party is an individual.

Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.
Examples of court- or government-appointed fiduciary account types are:
Lottery
Attorney client trust
Business trust
Estate - Nonindividual personal representative
Real-estate trust
Representative payee
Individual and nonindividual guardian or conservator
Individual and nonindividual receiverships
Statutory client trust
Note: The minimum deposit amount is always required for a time deposit account.
A corporation can have a single owner.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text: The Customer Identification Program (CIP) requirement is designed to enable the bank to form a reasonable belief about an individual’s and nonindividual’s true identity for all new and existing deposit accounts, loans, financial products, contracts, safe deposit boxes, or any other type of banking service or product. The process of forming a reasonable belief is taking steps to verify the identity, credentials, identification, and other supporting information provided by potential and existing customers. You must provide the required disclosures, notices, and information to potential and existing customers.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
The Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirement enables Cayman Bank to know its customers and understand the nature and purpose of accounts and relationships to develop a customer risk profile.
Refer to the CSBB 1FC Program Document for additional details on Sanctions situations, UAR submission, CIP requirements, CDD requirements, and Beneficial Ownership requirements.
Compare the provided customer information to the customer identification (ID) or proof-of-entity documentation.
A completed Certification Regarding Beneficial Owners of Legal Entity Customers form must be obtained, certified, and signed by the customer at new account opening or business customer relationship maintenance to be valid and acceptable. Reference:CIP and CDD Resources

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
When opening a business deposit account, at least one owner or key executive with entity authority and control must have a TIN (for example, SSN or ITIN). If they do not, the business account cannot be opened
A customer request to open a new deposit account must not be declined for the: Account may be open only a short time Customer has or will have duplicate accounts

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Employees may open business deposit accounts for customers meeting the following criteria: Are nonindividual entity customers (including sole proprietorships, business trusts, business pension or profit-sharing trust, corporations, limited-liability companies, limited-liability partnerships, joint venture, general partnerships, social and recreational clubs, unincorporated associations and civic groups). Have gross annual sales of less than $2 million. Do not require Treasury Management Services. Do not have complex lending needs.
If the business does not meet the criteria, the employee must refer the customer to the appropriate partner or affiliate.
Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Disclosures: If disclosures are not available, the account cannot be opened. A supply of disclosure New Account Kits (NAKs) may be obtained from another location. If the customer wants to receive the disclosure electronically and has access to their email through their mobile device, the account can be opened.
Employees must not sign or otherwise place a customer’s signature on a document on the customer’s behalf or in lieu of the customer physically signing. Print or digital copies of signatures obtained from the customer on previous documents must not be used when a signature is required on a new document.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Employees are prohibited from entering into any customer provided agreements, up to and including agreements barring Branch Banking from sharing due diligence information with Financial Crimes Risk Management (FCRM), Internal Audit, regulators, or other similar functions. Any existing accounts with external agreements identified after account opening will be immediately exited.
When opening a new account for a business, the individuals who provide personal financial information in connection with the business must be given the opportunity to elect whether to share personal information with other Cayman Bank affiliates.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Treasury Management deposit products are restricted from being offered to customers (for example, Controlled Disbursement, Stagecoach deposit). Only business account products can be opened by branch employees. Refer to the Products database for currently available accounts. Referrals must be directed to the appropriate partner or affiliate.
Related procedure: Referrals to Partners or Affiliates
Employees must not travel outside of the U.S. for purposes of conducting bank business or discussing bank related products or services.
Do not open a new account requiring Cayman Bank to provide escrow services. Tell the customer the account cannot be opened.
Exception: For Benefit Of (FBO)- Title Escrow Service Agreement can be opened.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
A new account request must be blocked or restricted if the transaction is conducted by, for, or on behalf of countries, entities, or individuals affected by the Foreign Assets Control regulations.
When the tax-responsible customer (for example, business account owner, third party, client, or insolvent party) is an entity, trust, or estate formed in a U.S. territory, a noninterest-earning product must be used.
Prohibited high-risk industries are not permitted to open or maintain deposit accounts or Safe Deposit Box Relationships.
Deposit accounts and Safe Deposit Box Relationships for restricted high-risk industries can be opened after they have been reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence Center (EDDC).

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Certain unregulated or unlicensed financial institutions are prohibited from being opened or maintained in Branch Banking. These industries must be reviewed and approved by Enhanced Due Diligence prior to opening the account.
If a due diligence review is required, and the customer indicates either of the following, a Suspected Risk Referral (SRR) must be submitted, and a new account request must be denied: Refuses to provide information required to complete due diligence. Suspiciously indicates they provided the wrong responses to the compliance questions after the banker already disclosed the enhanced diligence requirements to the customer.
Multiple signature requirements are not allowed on a deposit account.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
A fee waiver must not be placed on an account only because the customer has objected to the standard fees.
A Payable on Death (POD) beneficiary may only be added to an account if the entity is a sole proprietorship, and is not an IOLTA, RETA or public fund account. Other types of business entities (for example, corporations, partnerships, or limited liability companies) are ineligible for a POD beneficiary.
First deposit for new account: The minimum deposit requirement must be met and made at the time of the account opening.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Exception: When a court- or government-appointed fiduciary indicates funds are not available to be deposited to the new account but will be deposited in the future, a minimum deposit is not required. Tell the customer the account must be funded within 30 calendar days, or it may be subject to closure.
Examples of court- or government-appointed fiduciary account types are:
Lottery
Attorney client trust
Business trust
Estate – Nonindividual personal representative
Real-estate trust
Representative payee
Individual and nonindividual guardian or conservator
Individual and nonindividual receiverships
Statutory client trust
Note: The minimum deposit amount is always required for a time deposit account.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Before opening a deposit account, risk screening must be completed on the following individuals: Owners with 25% or more ownership that have entity authority and control Key executives with entity authority and control
Note: Owners with less than 25% entity ownership with authority and control added to the business relationship will also be risk screened but it is not required.
Exception: Risk screening is not required for the following individuals:
Nonindividual owners with or without entity authority and control
Individual owners without entity authority and control
Key executives of a U.S. government unit or agency, or Indian tribal government

section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
All sanctions-related actions should only be performed as directed by FC Risk Management and the Global Sanctions Screening and Reporting Group (GSSRG) team.
The following not all-inclusive list is examples of how to identify a nexus (connection) to Cuba, Iran, or North Korea.
Self-Identify: Conversing with the individual and they provide that information (for example, while completing a transaction request, answering country of citizenship or address questions)
Document Review: Reviewing identification or other documentation the customer provides (for example, Iran Passport, U.S. Passport stating the place of birth is Cuba, proof of address)
If you identify any red flags or unusual activity, submit an SRR.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
The Emerging Portfolio Customer Support Team must be contacted at 1-866-902-9181 when a federal, state, or local government entity requests public funds checking, savings, or time deposit account.
Note: Due to the complexity of these types of accounts, tell the customer the account opening process may take 3 to 5 business days. Ensure all documentation is obtained and provided to RBRM Operations, and all customer identifications are completed to avoid adding additional days to the processing time.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Public funds business deposit product accounts are opened by RBRM on branch employee’s behalf. After the account is on the system, RBRM will transfer the account to the branch. For account maintenance inquiries and requests for government entity public fund accounts, reference the appropriate account maintenance branch procedures.
Accounts owned by a federal, state or local government entity or instrumentality must be in a public funds product.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:
Exception: Government entities opening an account using a Tax Identification Number (TIN) [for example, Social Security Number (SSN), Employer Identification Number (EIN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN)] other than their own for purposes of holding funds on behalf of another non-governmental entity or individual.
When opening a deposit account an employer identification number (EIN) for the federal, state, or local government entity must be obtained.

title: Business Deposit Account: Estate, Receivership, Government Entities, Business Trusts, Girl Scouts - PR1779
section: Government entities > Understand the rules
text:

title: Savings Bonds: Rate and Redeem - PR1949
section: Summary
text:
Rate and redeem full, half-sheet, series E, EE, or I savings bonds, including identifying presenters, resolve scanning issues, remove or reverse bonds, and special handling procedures.
Select the section heading to expand the procedure content.

title: Savings Bonds: Rate and Redeem - PR1949
section: Understand the rules
text:
Confirm the presenter is a consumer customer with an open and active Cayman Bank checking, savings, or time account (CD), for 12 months or longer.
Note: If the account has been opened less than 12 months, you may redeem bonds up to $1,000 per day (aggregate redemption value). If the total cash redemption value is more than $1,000, the customer has the following bond redemption options:
Redeem the bonds up to the allowable $1,000 total value and take back the remaining bonds.
Redeem all bonds at full value using the Treasury Direct website.

title: Savings Bonds: Rate and Redeem - PR1949
section: Understand the rules
text:
Exception – Customer eligible for The Private Bank Experience: The $1,000 allowable redemption amount does not apply to customers who are eligible for The Private Bank Experience regardless of how long the account has been opened.
Do not redeem bonds payable to a business or trust.
The U.S. Department of the Treasury prohibits a bank from charging a fee to redeem a U.S. savings bond.
If issued in a foreign country, the death certificate must be the original or a certified copy.

title: Savings Bonds: Rate and Redeem - PR1949
section: Understand the rules
text: If redeeming multiple bonds within the same transaction, the customer must sign each bond. Basic transaction information can be documented on one bond and is not required to be written on every bond in the transaction. Any additional required documentation for unique situations as detailed in the procedure below must be written on each bond (for example, name change reason, beneficiary, decedent information). The following information may be written on only one bond when multiple bonds are presented:

change reason, beneficiary, decedent information). The following information may be written on only one bond when multiple bonds are presented: Identification Social security number (SSN) (if the printed SSN on the front of the bond does not belong to the customer) Customer's current address Type of Cayman Bank account Last 4 digits of the account number Date the account was opened
Tell the customer when additional time or assistance is required to review the transaction.
Transaction approvers: Introduce yourself to the customer and explain your role when you are asked to review a transaction or request.

Transaction approval guide

text: Owner: Owner with a beneficiary | Example registration: John A. Smith POD Jane Johnson The person named first owns the bond and may endorse and redeem it. If the owner dies, the beneficiary automatically becomes the sole owner. The registration says "POD" standing for "PAYABLE ON DEATH."

section: Reverse a transaction with a savings bond
text:
TellerView typically allows transaction reversals within 1 hour of completion or until the batch is closed for transactions included in a batch, whichever occurs first. After one hour, you cannot return the physical savings bond to the customer because bond processing has begun. Note: When the bond from a reversed transaction is returned to the customer and has been branded, stamped, or signed, the customer must contact Treasure Direct to redeem the bond. Related procedure:Search the Electronic Journal and Reverse Teller Transactions
Access the T621 EJ Search.
Search for the applicable transaction (Item Cashing [T100], Deposit [T200] or Purchase Bank Check [T400]) in which the bonds were processed.

text:

Place the bond in a clear document carrier and rescan.
Reference: Item scanning - teller reference guide

Cancel the original transaction.
On the teller system, access T521 and complete all applicable fields by manually typing the MICR line information on the Bond Detail screen.

text:

title: Copy Requests: Statements, Debit or Credit Items, and Account Documentation - PR2306
section: Understand the rules
text:
The customer must have authority to request this transaction.
A copy of a previously deposited payment slip is only available for legal purposes (for example, an IRS audit).
If the requestor is a non-Prime or Premier Checking account owner requesting a copy of a statement, provide only the pages related to the non-Prime or Premier Checking account owner.
If an owner was removed and the account remains open, the former owner can only request copies for the time period during which they were an owner.

section: Requests for printed account information
text:
Never encourage or suggest a customer to share online banking credentials with others to access account information.
Do not accept customer requests to email or mail account information directly to third-party individuals or entities without transaction authority on the requested account.
Requests for account information may be verbally communicated to the customer or a printed copy may be provided.

section: Summary
text:
Request or provide a teller transaction approval or process an assisted approval, self-approval, teller override or self-override on TellerView.
Select the section heading to expand the procedure content.

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules
text: If your Employee ID was used to approve a transaction that you did not authorize, refer to the Fraud Claims and Identity Theft: Unusual Transactions or Account Activity, Elder and Vulnerable Adult Financial Exploitation procedure. Notify Branch Management Report suspected employee misconduct through the Cayman Bank EthicsLine Web Reporting System as soon as possible, but no later than the end of the same calendar day the activity or behavior is discovered

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules
text: When a transaction review or approval is required: Tell the customer when additional time or assistance is required to review the transaction. Transaction approvers: Introduce yourself to the customer and explain your role when you are asked to review a transaction or request. Before attempting to approve or obtain approval for a transaction, always complete a review of all transaction items, all system warning messages, and the Risk Evaluation Tool, when required. Note: System messages for the transaction may be reviewed by selecting Go Back on the Override screen.

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules
text:
Transaction approval or reference codes obtained from another department (for example, Treasury Management Client Services [TMCS], The Private Bank [TPB]) must be documented in the Comments field on the Approval screen (for example, TPB code AB12345).
Related procedures:
Risk Evaluation: Deposits, Foreign Currency Orders, Item Cashing, and Negotiable Instruments
Transactional Safeguards and Exceptions
References:
Prevent losses with a risk evaluation
TellerView system messages tool
Transaction approval guide
Branch Banking de-escalation guide

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules > Transactional exceptions
text:
When a transactional exception is being approved (for example, waiving the identification requirement for a transaction), the exception must be documented on the Approval screen in the Comments field.
When the Approval screen is not available, document the transaction exception on the item and scan or re-scan into TellerView to capture the approval.
Approvers must not make exceptions to transactions they are processing (no self-approvals are permitted).
Only branch management or regional employees may approve transactional exceptions.
Transactional exceptions cannot be made for Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) regulatory procedure requirements. These requirements ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements.

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules > Transactional exceptions
text: Item cashing transactions only: Select the Other approval reason option when approving a transactional exception.

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules > Remote approvals
text:
When a remote approval is required (transaction exceeds the transaction authority of all employees currently in the branch), call the remote approver to ensure they are available to review and approve the transaction. This will also allow the remote approver to obtain required transaction information.
Remote approvers will receive an approval request notification email and are required to take the following action based on email access at the time of the transaction: Reference: TellerView Remote Approval Reference Guide
Note: If a delay occurs in receiving the approval email, use the No email access process to complete the transaction for the best customer experience.

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules > Remote approvals
text: Email access: Transaction approved: Complete one of the following actions: Select the I approve link Verbally provide the 6-digit authorization code. Note: If there is more than a 60 second delay in the systematic approval of the transaction using the I approve link, ask the teller to select the Approver does not have access to email checkbox and follow the No email access process. Transaction declined: Verbally decline the transaction and select I do not attest.

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules > Remote approvals
text:
No email access at the time of the transaction: Transaction approved: Verbally approve the transaction. Complete the notification email approval attestation by selecting I Attest before the end of the same business day. Transaction not approved: Verbally decline the transaction. Complete the notification email decline decision attestation by selecting I do not attest before the end of the same business day.
Notes:
The remote approver will receive a confirmation of their selected decision (I approve, I attest, or I do not attest).

title: Approvals and Overrides – Teller - PR2321
section: Understand the rules > Remote approvals
text:
A BSP Alert will be generated when the transaction approval attestation is not completed by the end of the day the transaction was approved and processed or when you select the I do not attest link but the transaction was processed using your credentials.
If your Employee ID was used to remote approve a transaction that you did not authorize, refer to the Fraud Claims and Identity Theft: Unusual Transactions or Account Activity, Elder and Vulnerable Adult Financial Exploitation procedure:
Notify Branch Management

Transaction approval: From a Branch Banking employee (listed on the Approver menu or selected from the Search for Approver field on the Approval screen). Notes: TellerView will only allow Branch Banking employees with the appropriate transaction approval authority on Banker Profile to approve deposit, item cashing, purchase bank check, branch settlement, and debit memo post transactions. Do not attempt to use the employee from the other line of business (for example TPB, TMCS) as the approver on TellerView.
Obtain an approval or reference code by calling the proper department or other line of business (for example TPB, TMCS).

title: Payment Maintenance: Consumer and Small Business Lending - PR472
section: Summary
text: Handle customer requests related to payment maintenance for consumer and small business lending accounts. Assist with payoff and paydown quotes, deferrals, extensions, re-ages, rewrites, and changes to payment options or amounts.

title: Payment Maintenance: Consumer and Small Business Lending - PR472
section: Understand the rules
text:
The customer must have authority to request this transaction.
Do not:Give printed SVP, Hogan, or Shaw screens with payment, payoff, or transaction information to customers. Process incoming phone requests to move funds.
Line of credit, credit card, and loan account payments received in the branches will receive credit for the payment effective on the day the customer made the payment.
A business cannot request or require an active duty servicemember to use a military allotment to repay an obligation secured by tangible and moveable personal property.
All new personal loans accounts receive billing statements rather than coupon books.

title: Payment Maintenance: Consumer and Small Business Lending - PR472
section: Understand the rules
text:
Accounts that qualify for non-monthly payments receive a billing statement according to the frequency of the payment schedule.
Refer to the Unusual Activity Referral (UAR) Requirements procedure when you suspect unusual activity.
If the customer alleges a Cayman Bank employee opened the account without their consent (unauthorized), or the account features or terms do not align with details discussed with the Cayman Bank employee at account opening (unwanted):Immediately contact the appropriate department using the banker-facing phone numbers listed below to review options for the account closure. Tell the processing department the closure reason is due to the account being unauthorized or unwanted and related to sales practices allegations.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Summary
text: Maintain and certify a customer's TIN, TIN type, or foreign status on Form W-9 or Form W-8BEN, and reverse or refund current year backup federal tax withholding on an interest earning deposit account.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text:
Do not: Provide tax advice to a customer. Refer them to their tax advisor or to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for assistance.
Example: Customer asks for a tax status.
Apply for a TIN on behalf of a customer or assist customers with applying for a TIN or provide advice regarding the application process. Refer them to their tax advisor, the IRS, or to their local Social Security Administration (SSA) office for assistance.
The customer must have authority to request this transaction.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text:
Only the following individuals have authority to certify a TIN on an account: Consumer account: Primary tax-responsible account owner and individuals authorized to certify on the customer’s behalf (for example, POA, signer on minor-by account, trustee) Business account: An owner, partner, or key executive with transaction authority on the account
If a U.S. citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident, or customer who is considered a U.S. person for tax purposes is a joint owner on an account with a non-U.S. person or non- U.S. entity, the U.S. person or U.S. entity must be the primary tax-responsible owner on the account.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text: A TIN may have the same digits as another TIN if the TIN type is different. Example: An employer identification number (EIN) may be the same digits as a Social Security number (SSN).

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text: For stateless customer: W-9 generated by SVP does not require additional action. W-8BEN will be created with Stateless listed as the country of citizenship. This is considered invalid by the IRS, which will result in 24% interest withholding. To create or replace the form with a valid form. Access and manually complete a Substitute Form W-8BEN (596034). Ask the customer to review the IRS form completion instructions for country of citizenship and provide a country meeting the criteria. If the customer indicates they are a U.S. citizen or resident alien, complete a Substitute Form W-9 (595925) instead. Scan the manually completed and signed form to replace the invalid form.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text: A W-9 form is generated for the following: U.S. citizens. Non-U.S. citizens who satisfy the green card test and have lawful U.S. permanent residency status. They are issued a TIN and a Permanent Resident Card or Resident Alien Card. Non-U.S. citizens who do not have U.S. permanent residency status but satisfy the substantial presence test. Days present while holding a special visa, for example a student or diplomatic visa, are not counted. If the customer is unsure whether they meet the substantial presence test: Refer the customer to their Tax Advisor.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text:
counted. If the customer is unsure whether they meet the substantial presence test: Refer the customer to their Tax Advisor. Ask them to visit irs.gov and search for the current revision of Publication 519, which provides additional details on the requirements of the substantial presence test.
Notes:
Resident aliens are typically treated as U.S. Persons for tax purposes if they meet the Green Card or Substantial Presence Test. If they complete a W-8BEN and have a U.S. mailing address, it will be treated as invalid unless they provide documentation supporting their non-U.S. status, for example a student visa or diplomatic visa.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text:
It is the customer’s responsibility to review the tax rules around the substantial presence test and determine if they have been in the U.S. long enough to be treated as a U.S. person from a tax perspective. If the customer states, they do not meet the substantial presence test than they can sign a W-8BEN instead.
A W-8BEN is generated for non-U.S. citizens who live in the U.S. temporarily. They may or may not have a U.S. TIN. They should have a permanent home or principal establishment in a foreign country.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text: Note: If a U.S. address was provided at account opening, other documentation must be presented to demonstrate the customer is a resident of a foreign country, for example a student or diplomatic VISA or a passport.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text: A W-9 or W-8BEN does not generate for customers with no SSN or ITIN but has a permanent resident status in the U.S. or who is a U.S. person based on the IRS substantial presence test. Customers may have expired foreign documentation or documentation that indicates they are living in the U.S. They no longer have a permanent home or principal establishment in a foreign country. This customer will be subject to 24% withholding and form 1099 reporting on interest earned because they cannot provide an SSN or ITIN.

title: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Foreign Status Maintenance, Certification, and Backup Withholding - PR607
section: Understand the rules
text:
To limit the bank's risk and exposure a business decision has been made to restrict the products available to customers who are subject to the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA).
Accounts for business entities, trusts, and estates formed in a foreign country are prohibited in Regional Banking.
Complete a Suspected Risk Referral (SRR) for suspicious or unusual behavior or if customer gives minimal or possibly false information that you cannot verify (for example, EIN, SSN, TIN, individual tax identification number [ITIN]).

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Summary
text:
Branches with an approved coin-counting machine only: Sell full bags of coin from the coin-counting machine to the branch vault, perform a weekly balance or monthly random cash count on the coin-counting machine in dual control, and complete monthly testing.
Select the section heading to expand the procedure content.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Understand the rules
text:
Coin-counting machines must be:Used for U.S. coin only. Located in a secure area. Maintained, accessed, and locked in dual control. Locked at all times.
Exception: Branches with written approval from the Branch Manager may leave the coin-counting machine unlocked during business hours. A copy of the completed and approved Coin Counting Machine Exception Approval (596391) form must be maintained in the branch Security File.
Reference:Records Management > Retention Schedule
Complete coin machines tasks using the appropriate level of control:Weekly balancing and random monthly cash counts: Dual control Monthly coin-counting machine testing: Single control

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Understand the rules
text:
Adhere to all dual control requirements in the Dual Control and Single Control procedure when completing dual control tasks associated with maintaining, accessing, and balancing the coin counting machine.
Employees must have appropriate authorities in Banker Profile:Vault Access authority to sign on to the vault cashline (00 or 50) Dual Control authority to be part of a dual control team
Sell full coin bags from coin-counting machines to the branch vault cashline (00 or 50).
Complete all steps to sell coin bags to the branch vault consecutively, including applicable TellerView transactions, while maintaining dual control.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Understand the rules
text:
Rotate the following tasks according to the applicable rotation frequency requirements in the Dual Control and Single Control procedure:Weekly coin-counting machine balancing Monthly random cash counts of the coin-counting machine Monthly testing of the coin-counting machine
Note: Refer to the Random Cash Counts Dashboard on the Bank Supervision – Reporting site on Branch Portal to view previous dual control teams or TellerView T657 View All Cash Lines to see the last two dual control teams who completed random cash counts on the coin-counting machine cashline.
The maximum amount of coin that can be stored overnight in a single coin-counting machine is $5,250.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Understand the rules

Assign user IDs, keys, and combinations on Security Control.

Refer to your equipment procedures for processing loose coin through the coin machine. See your manager if you are unsure of these steps.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Sell coins to Branch Vault
text:
In dual control, remove each full bag from the coin-counting machine and ensure it is:Sealed. Kept out of customer view. Placed in a locked unit or compartment in the branch vault as soon as possible.
Place an empty coin bag on the coin machine to replace the full bag.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Sell coins to Branch Vault
text:
Sign on to the applicable cashline in dual control and select T611 Buy Sell Cash to sell all coin bags removed to the vault cashline (00 or 50).Select the compartment where the coin will be stored. Complete the Cash Detail screen, by denomination (not a lump sum), for the compartment selected. Select Add Compartment and repeat steps a and b if coin bags will be stored in multiple compartments. Select Submit. Enter dual control credentials.
Secure each sealed coin bag in the branch vault compartment selected in the T611 transaction until ready for shipment.
Related procedure:Outgoing Currency and Coin Shipments

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Weekly balance
text:
Balance all coin-counting machines in dual control at least weekly. If an employee completes a buy/sell transaction after balancing and before Perm Off, rebalance the cashline on TellerView.
Ensure all employees complete their buy/sell transactions on TellerView before balancing.
Obtain the balancing information from the coin-counting machine in dual control.
Sign on to the appropriate coin-counting machine cashline on TellerView in dual control.
Select T614 Balancing.
Enter each coin denomination amount. Do not enter a lump sum.
Select Daily in the Counting For drop-down menu and enter the balancing information.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Weekly balance
text:
Determine if the cashline balances:Balances or has a difference of $3 or less: Select Ok. Does not balance: TellerView automatically navigates to the cash difference transaction. Follow the steps in the Balancing: Drop and Go, Teller, and Vault > Process a cash difference on TellerView procedure.
Complete a Perm Off when balancing is complete.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Random monthly cash count
text:
Follow requirements for random monthly cash counts in the Cash Counts and Random Monthly Cash Detail > Unannounced random monthly cash count procedure.
Obtain the balancing information from the machine in dual control.
Sign on to the appropriate coin-counting machine cashline on TellerView in dual control.
Select T614 Balancing.
Enter each coin denomination amount (not a lump sum).
Select Shared in the Counting For drop-down menu and enter the balancing information.
Select Random Monthly in the Reason for Count drop-down menu.

title: Coin-Counting Machines: Sell Full Coin Bags, Balance, Test - PR63
section: Random monthly cash count
text:
Determine if the cashline balances:Balances or has a difference $3 or less: Go to the next step. Does not balance: If the difference cannot be resolved:Complete the File Out of Balance screen to process the difference. In the Comments field, provide details to explain the difference, if known, using acronyms in the Balancing: Drop and Go, Teller, and Vault > Process a cash difference procedure.
Follow the system prompts to enter dual control credentials and submit the balance.
Complete a Perm Off when complete.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Dual control requirements
text:
Complete activities associated with receiving, verifying, and securing incoming cash shipments in dual control in a secure area.
Employees responsible for cash shipments must have Dual Control authority on their Authority Record.
One of the employees must also have Vault Access authority.
Complete all steps for receiving and verifying a shipment while maintaining dual control, including associated TellerView transactions.
Counting incoming shipment cash, including bundle and strap counting currency, may be done by one employee with the second employee observing. If a discrepancy is identified, the second employee must count the cash while the first employee observes, to confirm if the first employee’s count is accurate.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Dual control requirements
text: If your branch does not have a desktop workstation inside the vault to process the shipment on TellerView:Secure and lock all cash in a dual-control compartment before leaving the vault to process TellerView transactions. TellerView transactions can be completed at the same time, separate from the physical transfer of cash to vault compartments where the shipment will be stored.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Contact armored transportation
text:
Email armoredtransportation@Cayman Bank.com if there are issues with the armored courier. In the email, include:
Your branch AU

What you were expecting in the shipment, for example the amount of currency and coin by denomination

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Allow courier access to secure area
text:
The armored courier must be identified each time they visit, even if it is the same courier week after week.
Do not require an armored courier to wait in a customer line or lobby. Identify them and escort them to a secure area as soon as possible.
Allowing a courier access to a secure area may be done in single control.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Allow courier access to secure area
text: Review the armored courier’s identification cards and identify them according to the vendor’s identification policy each time they visit. If the armored courier does not have identification or will not provide identification, do not allow them access to a secure area and do not accept the incoming shipment. Email armoredtransportation@Cayman Bank.com to report the armored courier according to instructions in the Contact armored transportation section.Brinks: Review both the identification card and signature card. Garda: Review both the front and back of the authorized agent card. Loomis: Review both the identification card and signature card. Axiom: Review both the identification card and signature card. title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Receive shipment from courier
text:
Complete steps in this section in dual control in a secure area.
If a T801 Incoming Shipment > Create Shipment was created in error, do not Receive or Reject the shipment in TellerView. It will automatically be removed from the T801 screen after approximately one week.
Follow the Separation of dual-control vault cash procedure to ensure you separate cash appropriately.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Receive shipment from courier
text:
If the courier must make multiple trips into the branch with an incoming shipment, until the courier has brought in all cash, remain in dual control in a secure area with the first shipment bags or boxes of coin. Only begin inspecting the bags of currency and boxes of coin in the presence of the courier. Only sign for cash you’ve received and inspected.
If the courier delivers customer deposit bags with an incoming branch cash shipment, ensure the branch cash shipment is processed and secured before completing the T682 Courier Delivered Log transaction.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Receive shipment from courier
text: Inspect the bags of currency and boxes of coin before the courier leaves the branch. Confirm the bags of currency belong to your AU.Reject and do not accept extra bags of currency or boxes of coin delivered in error. If the courier refuses to take extra boxes of coin or bags of currency delivered in error, do not reject the entire shipment. Accept the extra bag of currency or box of coin and process it according to this procedure, separate from other boxes of coin or bags of currency received. Do not open or use the extra bag of currency or box of coin delivered in error.

Carefully inspect all sides of the shipping bags for signs of tampering.Pull at the seams of the bag, looking for tears or cuts. Look for clear tape on the bag or small holes. Confirm the bag is sealed correctly.
Reject and do not accept bags of currency or boxes of coin with evidence of tampering. Note: Failure to identify a tampered bag may result in a loss to your branch.
Bundle or strap-count the currency through the bag to calculate a bag total and count boxed coin.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Receive shipment from courier
text: Sign the courier’s PDA device for the amount of cash accepted from the courier. If your courier does not have a PDA device, they will provide a paper manifest for you to sign.If the amount accepted is different than the PDA device or manifest, ask the courier to update the PDA device or manifest or provide a new paper manifest for the amount received. If the courier cannot update their PDA and doesn’t have a paper manifest, refuse the shipment and contact Armored Transportation. Maintain possession of shipments in dual control after the shipment has been reviewed, signed for, and taken from the armored courier.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Verify the shipment
text:
Complete all steps in this section in dual control in a secure area.
Verify the shipment in dual control on the same day it is delivered.Cayman Bank cash vault: Report discrepancies by the end of the same day the shipment is received. Outsourced cash vault (Loomis or Garda is printed on the Cash In Transit ticket received): Report discrepancies no later than 2:00 p.m. Mountain Time the following business day. Federal Reserve: Report discrepancies immediately after identifying them.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Verify the shipment
text:
If the shipment bag was opened to remove the Cash in Transit (CIT) ticket, the same dual control employees who opened the shipment bag to remove the CIT ticket must complete the T802 Verify/Break Down Shipment transaction.
Branches servicing ATMs: Move ATM cash listed on the iCom Order Details into TellerView ATM ID compartments on your incoming shipment day. Failure to do so will negatively impact future cash ordering forecasts for both branch and ATM cash.
Follow the Separation of dual-control vault cash procedure to ensure you separate cash appropriately.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Verify the shipment
text:
Open the shipment bags and remove the currency. Exception: Do not open or use extra bags of currency or boxes of coin delivered in error. Bundle and strap count the currency through the bag to complete the verification process.
Count the currency (bundle or strap count) and boxed coin. Consider documenting the amounts by denomination for entry in TellerView.
Complete the following if you identify:
Loose currency because a strap broke
Currency straps stamped by another Cayman Bank branch
Blank currency straps

section: Verify the shipment
text:

Refer to the Process Suspected Counterfeit Bills, Unfit, Mutilated, or Contaminated Currency and Coin procedure if suspected counterfeit currency is found when detail counting currency.

title: Incoming Currency and Coin Shipments - PR7554
section: Verify the shipment
text: If the Verified amounts do not match the Amounts listed in shipment: Select No in the popup message. Recount the cash by denomination and validate entries are correct. Note: TellerView compares the Amounts listed in for shipment to the amounts you enter in the Verified amounts fields by individual denomination. Even if the Total amounts match, the popup message will display if individual denominations do not match. If amounts do not match after a recount, select Yes in the popup message. Note: If the Total amounts do not match, selecting Yes will adjust the compartment amount only. The vault cashline will be out of balance by the difference.

text:
Select the first compartment where cash will be stored and complete the Cash Detail by denomination (not a lump sum) for the cash to be stored there.
If cash will be stored in additional compartments, select Add Compartment and repeat step 8.
Select Submit when all currency and coin has been moved to the appropriate compartments and there are no Remaining Funds $ to move.
Enter dual control credentials.
Branches servicing ATMs: Complete a T805 Compartment Transfer transaction to transfer the iCom Order Details ATM Requirement amounts to the TellerView ATM ID compartment for the designated ATM.

Complete the Add Cash to the ATM section of the ATM: Servicing procedure if you are adding cash to the ATM at this time.
If you have not already done so, secure the currency and coin in the compartments selected in the T802 and T805 transactions.

section: Process cash discrepancies: Federal Reserve Bank
text:
MT and WY: Designated branches only.
Contact the Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) to report any differences between the currency amounts ordered and received. For example, the currency order is short a bundle or a strap is short bills. If requested by the FRB, access and complete the Difference Claim Request Form available at FedCash Services Forms.
Do not complete the steps in this section for a missing box of coin or bag of currency. Email armoredtransportation@Cayman Bank.com on the day the shipment is received to report the missing box of coin or bag of currency according to instructions in the Contact armored transportation section. Request a ticket number.
